title: Running totals
objective: Compute cumulative sums and counts with SUM() OVER (ORDER BY ...), reset them per group or per year with PARTITION BY, make them deterministic with tie-breakers, and turn them into cumulative %.
context: 'Where are we year-to-date?', 'How many customers have we acquired so far?', 'Which products make up 80% of revenue?' — all running totals. Finance reads YTD lines every day; merchandising uses cumulative share (Pareto) to decide which products to focus on.

exercises.title: Cumulative revenue through 2025
exercises.question: Finance wants to watch 2025 revenue accumulate month by month.
exercises.prompt: Gross revenue = SUM(quantity * unit_price) over the order_items of valid orders (order_status IN ('completed','shipped','returned')); cancelled and pending orders are excluded. For the months of 2025, return order_month ('YYYY-MM'), gross_revenue and running_revenue (sum of gross_revenue from 2025-01 through the current month), both rounded to 2 decimals, ordered by order_month.
hints: Aggregate to months first, then apply a window SUM.
Here filtering to 2025 *before* the window is what we want — the total should start in January 2025.
SUM(gross_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY order_month ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_revenue ... WHERE order_month >= '2025-01'
exercises.why: Window SUM over an ordered set is the running total — no self-join or correlated subquery needed.

recall.q: What frame gives a running total?
recall.a: ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW.

exercises.title: Customer base over time
exercises.question: Growth wants the cumulative number of signed-up customers after each signup.
exercises.prompt: Return customer_id, signup_date and customers_to_date (number of customers who signed up on or before this one, counting in order of signup_date then customer_id), ordered by signup_date, customer_id.
hints: A running count is COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY ...).
Add customer_id to the window ORDER BY as a tie-breaker in case two customers sign up the same day.
COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY signup_date, customer_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS customers_to_date
exercises.why: Cumulative counts (customers, subscribers, installs) are the 'total base' line on growth dashboards. ROW_NUMBER would give the same numbers here — COUNT generalises to filtered counts.

recall.q: Without a tie-breaker and with the default RANGE frame, what happens to two customers who signed up the same day?
recall.a: They are peers and both get the same (higher) running count.

exercises.title: Year-to-date revenue
exercises.question: The finance dashboard shows a YTD line that restarts every January.
exercises.prompt: Gross revenue = SUM(quantity * unit_price) over the order_items of valid orders (order_status IN ('completed','shipped','returned')); cancelled and pending orders are excluded. For all 24 months, return order_month ('YYYY-MM'), gross_revenue and ytd_revenue (running total that restarts each calendar year), both rounded to 2 decimals, ordered by order_month.
hints: A running total that 'restarts' = PARTITION BY the thing that restarts it.
The year is substr(order_month, 1, 4) (or strftime('%Y', ...) in the CTE).
SUM(gross_revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY substr(order_month, 1, 4) ORDER BY order_month ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS ytd_revenue
exercises.why: YTD, QTD and MTD are just running totals partitioned by year, quarter or month.

recall.q: How do you make a running total reset every year?
recall.a: PARTITION BY the year inside the OVER clause.

exercises.snowflake: PARTITION BY YEAR(order_month) (or DATE_TRUNC('year', order_month)) with a DATE month key.

exercises.title: Customer lifetime spend, order by order
exercises.question: CRM wants each customer's cumulative spend after every valid order (for loyalty tier triggers).
exercises.prompt: Valid orders are order_status IN ('completed','shipped','returned'); order_total = SUM(quantity * unit_price) of the order's items. For every valid order, return customer_id, order_id, order_date, order_total and cumulative_spend (running sum of order_total per customer, in order_date then order_id order), both rounded to 2 decimals. Ordered by customer_id, order_date, order_id.
hints: First collapse lines to one row per order (CTE with GROUP BY order).
PARTITION BY customer_id restarts the running sum for each customer.
SUM(order_total) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date, order_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_spend
exercises.why: Per-entity running totals drive thresholds: 'customer crossed $500 lifetime on order X'.

recall.q: What does PARTITION BY do to a running total?
recall.a: Restarts it for each partition (e.g. per customer).

exercises.title: Line-level running revenue (tie-breakers!)
exercises.question: Audit wants a line-by-line running revenue for Q4 2025 that matches the ledger exactly.
exercises.prompt: Valid orders are order_status IN ('completed','shipped','returned'). For each order line of valid orders with order_date from 2025-10-01 to 2025-12-31, return order_item_id, order_id, order_date, line_revenue (quantity * unit_price) and running_revenue (cumulative line_revenue in order of order_date, then order_item_id), both rounded to 2 decimals. Lines of the same order share a date, so each line must still get its own running value. Ordered by order_date, order_item_id.
hints: Several lines share an order_date. With ORDER BY order_date alone (default RANGE frame), they'd all show the same running value.
Add order_item_id to the window's ORDER BY and use a ROWS frame.
SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) OVER (ORDER BY o.order_date, oi.order_item_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_revenue
exercises.why: Non-deterministic window ordering produces numbers that change between runs or engines — a classic reconciliation headache. Always make the window ORDER BY unique.

recall.q: Two rows tie on the window ORDER BY under the default frame. What running value do they get?
recall.a: The same value: the total including both peers (RANGE frame treats ties as one step).

exercises.title: Progress toward the annual total
exercises.question: What share of 2025's full-year revenue had been booked by the end of each month?
exercises.prompt: Gross revenue = SUM(quantity * unit_price) over the order_items of valid orders (order_status IN ('completed','shipped','returned')); cancelled and pending orders are excluded. For the months of 2025, return order_month ('YYYY-MM'), gross_revenue, running_revenue (both rounded to 2 decimals) and pct_of_year = 100 * running_revenue / (total 2025 gross revenue), rounded to 1 decimal. Ordered by order_month.
hints: SUM(x) OVER () — no ORDER BY, no PARTITION — is the grand total on every row.
Divide the running total by that grand total; multiply by 100.0.
ROUND(100.0 * SUM(gross_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY order_month ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) / SUM(gross_revenue) OVER (), 1) AS pct_of_year
exercises.why: Two windows in one expression — a cumulative one and a total one — is the standard way to express 'progress toward a whole'. December must read 100.0.

recall.a: The total of x over the whole result set, repeated on every row.

exercises.snowflake: RATIO_TO_REPORT gives x / total; for cumulative share use SUM(...) OVER (ORDER BY ... ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) / SUM(...) OVER ().

exercises.title: Pareto: cumulative revenue share by product
exercises.question: Merchandising asks: how few products make up most of our revenue?
exercises.prompt: Gross revenue = SUM(quantity * unit_price) over the order_items of valid orders (order_status IN ('completed','shipped','returned')); cancelled and pending orders are excluded. For every product sold in a valid order, compute product_revenue. Return product_id, product_revenue, cumulative_revenue (running sum ordering products by product_revenue descending, then product_id ascending) — both rounded to 2 decimals — and cumulative_pct = 100 * cumulative_revenue / total revenue of all products, rounded to 1 decimal. Ordered by product_revenue descending, product_id.
hints: Aggregate revenue per product in a CTE.
The running total is ordered by revenue DESC (biggest first), with product_id as tie-breaker.
ROUND(100.0 * SUM(product_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY product_revenue DESC, product_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) / SUM(product_revenue) OVER (), 1) AS cumulative_pct
exercises.why: Pareto / ABC analysis is a running total over a *ranked* list rather than over time — the same window, a different sort key.

recall.q: In a Pareto table, what is the window ORDER BY?
recall.a: The measure descending (plus a unique tie-breaker), not a date.

exercises.snowflake: Add QUALIFY cumulative_pct <= 80 to keep only the 'A' products without another CTE.

worked_example.question: Show the cumulative number of orders (any status) by order date.
worked_example.sql:
SELECT order_id,
       order_date,
       COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY order_date, order_id
                      ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS orders_to_date
FROM orders
ORDER BY order_date, order_id
LIMIT 6;
worked_example.explanation: Each row counts itself plus all earlier rows. `order_id` is the tie-breaker: if two orders shared a date, each would still get its own running count.

recipe:
**Recipe: running total in 4 moves**

1. **Pick the grain** (one row per month, per order, per line) — pre-aggregate in a CTE if needed.
2. `SUM(measure) OVER (ORDER BY sort_key, tie_breaker ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)`.
3. **Reset** per group or period with `PARTITION BY` (per customer, per year → YTD).
4. **Cumulative %** = running total / `SUM(measure) OVER (PARTITION BY ...)` (a window with no ORDER BY = grand total).

```sql
SELECT order_month, gross_revenue,
       SUM(gross_revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY substr(order_month, 1, 4)
                                ORDER BY order_month
                                ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS ytd_revenue
FROM monthly;
```

**ROWS vs RANGE (the tie trap):** with only `ORDER BY` the default frame is
`RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW`, which treats rows with the *same* sort value as peers
and gives them all the same (end-of-tie) total. Add a unique tie-breaker (`ORDER BY order_date, order_item_id`)
and/or say `ROWS` explicitly so each row gets its own step.
snowflake_notes:
Window syntax is identical in Snowflake. Useful extras:

```sql
-- YTD with a DATE month key
SELECT order_month, gross_revenue,
       SUM(gross_revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY YEAR(order_month)
                                ORDER BY order_month
                                ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS ytd_revenue
FROM monthly;

-- cumulative share, and keep only the products that make the first 80% (QUALIFY = filter after windows)
SELECT product_id, product_revenue,
       SUM(product_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY product_revenue DESC, product_id
                                  ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING)
         / SUM(product_revenue) OVER () AS cumulative_share
FROM product_rev
QUALIFY cumulative_share <= 0.8;
```

- `RATIO_TO_REPORT(x) OVER (PARTITION BY ...)` = x / SUM(x) over the partition.
- `ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING` is shorthand for `ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` (SQLite accepts it too).
- `CONDITIONAL_TRUE_EVENT` / `CONDITIONAL_CHANGE_EVENT` are Snowflake-only helpers for running counts of events.
common_mistakes: Relying on the default RANGE frame with a non-unique ORDER BY — tied rows get identical running values.
Running-summing raw order lines when the question is per order or per month — pre-aggregate to the right grain first.
Forgetting PARTITION BY for YTD/per-customer totals, so the sum never resets.
Filtering out earlier periods when the running total is supposed to include them (or vice-versa) — decide where the accumulation starts.
Putting a window function inside WHERE — not allowed; use a CTE/subquery (or QUALIFY in Snowflake).
recall: Write the window clause for a per-customer running total.
SUM(x) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date, order_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW).
Default frame when a window has ORDER BY but no frame clause?
RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW (peers with equal sort values are included together).
How do you express cumulative % of total?
